content_preview.title: Valkey Project Benchmarks a Shared Valkey KV Cache for LLM Inference, Reporting 25% More Requests Served on the Same Two GPU Nodes
content_preview.summary: A Valkey blog post reports that a three-shard Valkey 9 cache served 4,631 requests versus 3,692 on the same two 8-GPU nodes, at a cost of about 15% on top of the GPU bill.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

A [Valkey project blog post](https://valkey.io/blog/kv-caching-on-valkey/) dated October 20, 2026, and written by Omer Rubinstein, Chaitanya Nuthalapati and Jeff Duffy, describes a benchmark in which a shared three-shard Valkey 9 cluster acted as an external cache for large language model (LLM) key-value (KV) data. According to the post, the same two GPU nodes served about 25% more requests with it than without it. The figures come from the authors' own benchmark of the project's ow...

recommendations: Published with a corrections record (two clarifications): current fix status of CVE-2026-105192 and author affiliations.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured Briefing, 710 words by body whitespace split (718 with link syntax stripped; range 300-800). Clear split between the post's claims, its stated limits, and what is not established. States that the benchmark is first-party, synthetic, single-configuration, with no independent replication found.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read snapshots source-0.html.gz (valkey.io blog), source-1.html.gz (cookbook README), source-2.html.gz (LMCache repo), then re-fetched live (WebFetch for the post; raw.githubusercontent.com README and docker-compose.yml via curl; GitHub API for the advisory) and relied on raw text. Source 0 (valkey.io blog, dated 2026-10-20, authors Omer Rubinstein, Chaitanya Nuthalapati, Jeff Duffy, footer 'Valkey contributors'): CONFIRMED setup (100 concurrent conversations growing 12K to 28K tokens, 8 req/s, two GPU nodes with 8 H100 each, Llama-3.1-70B, vLLM plus LMCache, only difference is a shared L2, three-shard Valkey 9 cluster, same AZ, synthetic traffic, 20 min run), table (3,692 vs 4,631 +25%; output tokens +28%; 11.9 vs 24.8 tok/s about 2.1x; first token 8.5 s vs 0.13 s for context under 16K with headroom; recompute about 10% vs about 1%), 6.5-10 GB per 20-30K token conversation, three limits ('Where it will not help'), noeviction and 20 GB host-memory cap. Quotes verified verbatim: 'cost about 15% on top of the GPU bill, so you pay 15% more to serve 25% more requests', 'stop costing you recomputes', 'rejects writes once memory is full'. Note the post's 25% is requests served in 20 minutes under a saturating synthetic load, which the article reports accurately. Source 1 (cookbook README): CONFIRMED four-container stack (valkey, lmcache-server, vllm-a, vllm-b), 'runs on CPU', 'over the multi-process connector', quote 'only covers what a single engine holds and is not shared with other engines' (the article's quotation ends at 'engines', verbatim), 'These examples use no authentication or TLS for simplicity.' Grep of README and the post for CVE/advisory/pickle: zero hits, so 'neither mentions the advisory' is accurate. Source 2 (LMCache repo): Apache-2.0, lists Redis/Valkey among storage backends, mentions the MP architecture; supports its use as the layer. Allowlist: github.com (line 1131) and valkey.io (line 1139) both present by exact hostname; no edit. Publisher check: the post is on the project's own site valkey.io, not a vendor site, so 'Valkey Project' is defensible; however two of three authors' bios identify them as AWS ElastiCache staff (Senior Technical Product Manager; product manager) and the third's handle is @omerrubi-amzn; the article does not mention this (clarification filed). Suspicious-pattern hits: source 0 excerpt '...re-sending retrieved documents and a big shared system prompt.' and source 1 excerpt '(a multi-turn chat, a shared system prompt, a reused RAG passage)' both matched system-prompt-reference. Read in context: ordinary technical prose about reusable prompt prefixes, no instruction directed at an AI agent. FALSE POSITIVES, scanner REJECT overridden. Source 2 had no hits. Independent sources: 0 (all first-party, disclosed in the article; Briefing so Analysis rules do not apply).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All numbers, names, dates and quotes match raw text. Setup description accurate. The inference that the CPU cookbook 'demonstrates cross-replica reuse rather than reproducing the H100 benchmark' is supported by the README's CPU statement and its stated walkthrough purpose. CVE cross-link: /article/2026-10/11-jfrog-reports-critical-lmcache-flaw-cve-2026-105192-... resolves to a published article (file exists in src/content/articles/2026-10) and the description of it ('critical flaw in LMCache's multiprocess mode, no fixed version listed as of October 7') matches that article and the JFrog page. Advisory facts checked against GitHub advisory GHSA-w5f2-9q9c-ff4h (published Oct 13, CVE-2026-105192): affected pip lmcache >= 0.3.9, < 0.5.6, patched 0.5.6 (PyPI shows 0.5.6 uploaded 2026-10-15; fix PR 5644 merged 2026-10-12); the flaw is in the multiprocess ZMQ transport, exposed when bound to a routable address. The article's statements are accurate as dated to October 7 but the article omits that a fix shipped in 0.5.6 before publication, which a reader could miss; clarification filed. For context only (not cited by the article, not published as a finding): the cookbook's docker-compose.yml pins lmcache==0.5.4, which falls inside the advisory's affected range, and runs the server with --host 0.0.0.0 on port 5555 without publishing that port to the host. The article's wording ('does not determine whether the cookbook's configuration is affected') neither implies nor denies exposure and is neutral; no person is blamed.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributed throughout ('according to the post', 'the authors say'). No promotional language; limits and the not-established section included. Cross-reference to the CVE is carefully worded and non-insinuating.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Herald article on Valkey KV caching or this post. Related coverage: the October 11 LMCache CVE article (linked) and the Valkey 9.x release articles; distinct topic.
concerns: Article reports the earlier CVE article's 'no fixed version as of October 7' status without noting the fix in 0.5.6 (advisory GHSA-w5f2-9q9c-ff4h, Oct 13; PyPI Oct 15). Recorded as a clarification.
Two of three post authors are identified in their bios as AWS ElastiCache staff; the article calls them the project's own contributors without noting this. Recorded as a clarification.
Single-vendor-adjacent, first-party, synthetic benchmark with no independent replication (disclosed in the article).
recommendations: For follow-ups on LMCache, check current advisory status (patched in 0.5.6) rather than the earlier article's October 7 snapshot.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully hedged Briefing; substantively sound with two minor clarifications. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurate first-party benchmark coverage of interest to a defined LLM-infrastructure audience, but a vendor-adjacent synthetic benchmark without replication
